reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the output contract, resource-assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, MedicationDispense resource-review context, deterministic aggregate, full structure finding inventory, fresh review decisions embedded in the structure report, and primary R4/R6 StructureDefinition and status CodeSystem facts for the central changed paths. Direct behavior reports had no MedicationDispense-specific findings; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior was treated as context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 MedicationDispense is trial-use/FMM 2, so the maturity baseline does not create strong anti-break pressure by itself. The practical concern instead comes from the clinical centrality of medication identity, subject, status, dosage instructions, and safety/audit links.

overall.oneLineConclusion: MedicationDispense keeps its identity, but core medication, status, subject, dosage, context, and safety-link changes make an R4-to-R6 migration program unavoidable while still leaving several low-cost preservation candidates worth revisiting.

reasoning.thesisMd: MedicationDispense is not removed or replaced, but R6 changes several central local paths in ways that raw R4 instances cannot satisfy: required `medication[x]` becomes required `CodeableReference` `medication`, `subject` becomes mandatory, the required modifier status code `stopped` becomes `unfulfilled`, repeating `Dosage` instructions become singleton `DosageDetails`, and contextual/safety paths are renamed, narrowed, or removed. That combination means practical migration requires explicit transforms, terminology mapping, and clinical or administrative policy decisions, not just validator or SDK refresh.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual migration shape is a major model remodel within a retained resource identity. Some transforms are mechanical for simple instances, such as wrapping medication concepts/references and renaming encounter-valued context, but several are not purely syntactic: missing subjects need a non-fabrication policy, status requires required-binding code mapping, multiple R4 dosage instructions must be merged or clinically reviewed for `DosageDetails`, EpisodeOfCare context has no direct R6 target, and performed-dispense `detectedIssue` links lose a local base home.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the central remodel already forces a converter for most serious implementations, preventing every local break is no longer the main migration lever. However, that does not make avoidable breaks unimportant. Low-cost preservation of a required status synonym, optional safety/audit links, old contextual meaning, or repeatable responsible parties would reduce validation failures and lossy policy decisions without blocking the broader R6 model.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest preservation candidates are `stopped` as a deprecated alias or explicit required-binding synonym for `unfulfilled`, retaining `detectedIssue` as a deprecated 0..* safety/audit link, preserving EpisodeOfCare context through a deprecated or separate optional element, and keeping `substitution.responsibleParty` repeatable while adding Organization. The medication and dosage remodels have higher tradeoffs because parallel old/new representations could create conflicting safety-critical medication or dosage data, so those are better treated as unavoidable migration chores unless official design rationale exposes a simpler compatibility path.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding in the supplied behavior reports affects MedicationDispense. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings are real ecosystem context, but they are not scored as MedicationDispense-specific resource-level breaks.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable = Yes`, `migrationShape = major-model-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. I agree with that resource-level posture, but for substantive rather than count-only reasons: the decisive facts are the concentration of remodels on required or safety-critical local paths and the existence of several independent avoidable preservation candidates.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the computable structural facts. Confidence is lower for standards intent because no official R4-to-R6 MedicationDispense diff, ballot rationale, live terminology expansion, or official ConceptMap was available in the supplied inputs.

findingConsiderations.title: Required medication choice element was replaced by required CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a central required wire-shape change from R4 `medicationCodeableConcept`/`medicationReference` to R6 `medication` CodeableReference. It makes raw R4 instances invalid and forces codegen and serializer changes. Because duplicate old/new medication representations would be safety-sensitive, this mostly supports the conclusion that migration is unavoidable rather than a simple low-cost preservation target.

findingConsiderations.title: MedicationDispense.subject became mandatory
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The subject is now required, so any R4 dispense without a patient/group is old-valid and new-invalid. Recipient identity is clinically fundamental, but migration still needs a policy for historical or partial records where subject cannot safely be inferred.

findingConsiderations.title: Required status binding replaced `stopped` with `unfulfilled` and changed CodeSystem canonical
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This required modifier status code appears to be a semantic rename: R4 `stopped` and R6 `unfulfilled` have materially the same definition. Since required bindings, generated enums, and status-driven workflows are affected, carrying `stopped` as a deprecated synonym or alias looks like a high-value, low-cost standards revisit even though a broader migration program is already needed.

findingConsiderations.title: statusReason[x] was renamed to notPerformedReason and converted to CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This optional path requires a rename and CodeableReference wrap. It contributes to the migration workload, but the R6 name is clearer for the existing non-performance meaning and preserving both old and new paths would introduce overlapping reason fields.

findingConsiderations.title: context was renamed to encounter and EpisodeOfCare target was removed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Encounter-valued R4 context can be renamed, but R4 EpisodeOfCare context has no direct R6 base target. If episode-level dispensing context remains clinically or administratively meaningful, preserving it through a deprecated or separate optional base element would avoid lossy migration at modest cost.

findingConsiderations.title: MedicationDispense.detectedIssue was removed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 allowed repeatable DetectedIssue links for actual or potential clinical issues associated with the dispense. R6 `notPerformedReason` only covers non-performance reasons, so completed-dispense safety/audit issues lose a direct local base element. This is an avoidable, safety-relevant removal worth standards review.

findingConsiderations.title: dosageInstruction changed from repeating Dosage array to singleton DosageDetails
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is one of the strongest migration drivers: R4 arrays of Dosage become a singleton DosageDetails object, and multiple or structured instructions may require clinical merge/review. The R6 safety goal is plausible, but the transform is not a simple local chore for real-world data.

findingConsiderations.title: substitution.responsibleParty changed from repeating to singleton and added Organization target
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Adding Organization is compatible in the R4-to-R6 direction, but reducing max from `*` to `1` can force lossy selection among responsible parties. Keeping repeatability while adding Organization would likely preserve old records with little base-model cost.

findingConsiderations.title: category became repeatable, binding weakened, and semantics broadened
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is mainly a widening/additional-expressiveness issue. It does not make R4 category data invalid in R6, so it should be handled as R6-to-R4 downgrade policy rather than a reason to revisit R6 base compatibility.

findingConsiderations.title: Several reference target domains widened, creating R6-to-R4 risks
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Widened targets for `partOf`, `performer.actor`, and `receiver` are forward-compatible for R4-to-R6 migration. They create downgrade constraints only when R6 uses new target types.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 added optional local elements with no direct R4 base element
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Optional additions such as `basedOn`, `statusChanged`, `fillNumber`, `recorded`, and `doseAdministrationAid` do not invalidate R4 instances. They require downgrade policy only for R6-to-R4 conversion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 narrows the `profile` input from `uri` to `canonical(StructureDefinition)`
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is shared Resource-level behavior context rather than a MedicationDispense-specific behavior break. It may affect servers validating MedicationDispense instances, but it should be reviewed and scored at the Resource behavior level, not duplicated into this resource conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit the `status` required binding change and consider preserving R4 `stopped` as a deprecated alias/synonym for R6 `unfulfilled`, with an explicit ConceptMap if the code rename remains.
Review safety/context preservation for removed or narrowed paths, especially `detectedIssue` and EpisodeOfCare-valued context, because both can require lossy migration despite being optional in R4.
Reconsider the `substitution.responsibleParty` max reduction separately from the useful Organization target addition; keeping repeatability would avoid forced loss in multi-party audit cases.

Publish migration guidance or maps for the unavoidable remodel: medication choice to CodeableReference, subject backfill/non-conversion policy, status mapping, `statusReason[x]` to `notPerformedReason`, and Dosage array to DosageDetails conversion with clinical-review triggers.

caveats: No official R4-to-R6 MedicationDispense diff or ballot rationale was available in the supplied inputs.
Terminology review used local CodeSystem/ValueSet files, not live expansion or version-alias behavior.
No official ConceptMap was available for status or structural conversion.
Narrative specification pages were not reviewed beyond computable StructureDefinition text.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only and not as direct MedicationDispense behavior findings.
